spikes.question: With DISCOVERY_MODE=search applied, can a client call a hidden tool directly by name, or does fastmcp refuse it so that every write must go through the call_tool proxy? Are always_visible (pinned) tools both listed and directly callable?
spikes.result: Hidden tools remain directly callable. tools/list advertises 3 tools (search_tools, call_tool, describe_tool) yet direct drawing_new, entity_create_line, drawing_info, entity_list and cad_batch all executed; only a non-existent name is refused, with fastmcp's generic 'Not found: Unknown tool'. BaseSearchTransform.get_tool (fastmcp/server/transforms/search/base.py:204-212) catches only the synthetic names and passes every other name to call_next; its docstring (:163) says 'Hidden tools remain callable'. CadSearchTransform.get_tool (discovery/transform.py:277-283) adds only describe_tool. _get_visible_tools (base.py:257-260) only builds the ranked list, it is not a call gate, and pinned tools are left out of the ranked list. With always_visible=[cad_batch, drawing_info, entity_list] tools/list has 6 entries and all are directly callable. Sizes (ratio/v1, chars/4.19): search as shipped 2,108 chars ~503 tokens; search + 3 pinned 11,437 chars ~2,730 tokens; full catalog 374,377 chars ~89,350 tokens. One entity_create_line request is 101 chars direct, 134 via call_tool (+33).
spikes.evidence: scratchpad/spikes/s1/probe_s1.py (in-memory fastmcp.Client against server.mcp, AUTOCAD_MCP_BACKEND=ezdxf); key lines: '[search_shipped] direct entity_create_line -> EXECUTED is_error=False', "[search_shipped] direct no_such_tool -> REFUSED ToolError: Not found: Unknown tool: 'no_such_tool'", '[search_pinned3] tools/list n=6', 'proxy overhead chars=33'.
spikes.decision: Positive for plan 1.8-11(d): nothing on the server forces writes through the proxy, so the search default can flip without a per-write wrapper cost; the real change is on the client side (hosts offer the model only listed tools), hence the migration note. The plan's 'search + pins <= 1,500 tokens' ceiling is not met by the three proposed pins (2,730, dominated by cad_batch's schema): 1.8-11 must either trim cad_batch's wire schema/description, pin fewer tools, or set the ceiling at the measured value. Not checked: whether a profile-hidden tool (e.g. solid_box with ENABLE_3D off) is still refused on a direct call; 1.8-11 adds that test.

spikes.question: Does a stdlib sqlite3 WAL journal (synchronous=NORMAL, busy_timeout=5000) survive the server process being killed (TerminateProcess)? Concurrency, per-record cost, folder effects?
spikes.result: 14 kills (8 in the scratchpad, 6 under %LOCALAPPDATA%\autocad-mcp-pro\state-spike) at random 50-500 ms: every logged commit read back (1-34 transactions, 5-170 rows per round), no partial or phantom transaction, parent open 6.9-13.4 ms (median 8.0 / 9.6 ms), first write 0.08-0.24 ms (no stale lock), integrity_check ok 14/14. The -wal/-shm files remain after a kill and the open does not checkpoint (main file stays 4096 B) until wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) or the last connection closes. Two writers: with busy_timeout=5000 the second waited 1,962 ms and succeeded; with 0 it failed at once with sqlite3.OperationalError 'database is locked' (SQLITE_BUSY, 5). Readers during ~100k commits in 2 s: 0 lock errors. Cost of a ~1 KB JSON row: INSERT+COMMIT median 11.1-12.4 us (p95 41-71 us) with NORMAL vs 353-383 us (p95 476-521 us) with FULL (~30x); UPDATE autocommit ~19 us vs ~355-412 us. Folder: same commit cost; under LOCALAPPDATA one first-open outlier of 48.8 ms against a 1.87 ms median (repeat run 0.68 ms median) - consistent with a one-time Defender scan, inferred not proven.
spikes.evidence: scratchpad/spikes/s2/s2_probe.py (subcommands kills | concurrency | readers | cost | opens); key lines: 'KILL_SUMMARY ... rounds 8 all_ok True open_ms median 8.01 max 9.37 wal_left 8 shm_left 8', 'CONC busy 5000 ... wait_ms 1961.9', "CONC busy 0 ... 'database is locked' SQLITE_BUSY 5", 'READERS busy 5000 reads 16 errors 0', 'COST NORMAL insert+commit_us median 12.1 p95 48.1', 'COST FULL insert+commit_us median 352.6 p95 488.0'.
spikes.decision: For 1.8-03: WAL + synchronous=NORMAL (a process kill loses nothing; only an OS crash or power loss can lose the last commits, which JOURNAL_SYNC=full covers). At open: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and assert the answer is 'wal'; busy_timeout=5000; synchronous=NORMAL; autocommit mode (isolation_level=None) with explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE so a lock upgrade cannot fail with SQLITE_BUSY; sweep rows still 'running' whose owner (pid + start time, stored on the row) is dead to unknown_commit, never rows of a live second server; optionally PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE). No integrity_check on every open (at most quick_check in a diagnostic). SQLITE_BUSY after the 5 s timeout is a journal-write failure recorded as such, never silent. Perf budget: ~12 us per commit (p95 ~70 us) plus ~20 us per state change, i.e. 30-40 us per operation, under 0.1 ms at p95; open once at startup 2-10 ms with ~50 ms outliers. Never FULL (~0.75 ms per operation).

spikes.question: Where does the 1.8-17(3) HTTP guard (Origin 403, Host 421, 8 MiB body 413, constant-time token compare, read-only token) plug into fastmcp 3.4.5 and into how server.py starts HTTP?
spikes.result: server.py: StaticTokenVerifier built at :543-554 (scopes mcp:read, mcp:write) and passed as FastMCP(auth=_auth) at :560-562; _validate_http_bind :13311, _effective_http_host :13348, _guarded_run_async :13386 wraps mcp.run_async on the instance (:13392) forwarding **kwargs; main() :13395 calls mcp.run() for stdio (:13404) else mcp.run(transport, host, port) (:13406-13411); no http_app( call. fastmcp 3.4.5: http_app(path, middleware: list[ASGIMiddleware], ..., host_origin_protection, allowed_hosts, allowed_origins) (mixins/transport.py:370); run_http_async(..., middleware=None, ...) calls self.http_app(middleware=...) (:328); run()/run_async() pass **transport_kwargs (:75, :109); no custom_middleware. User middleware is appended after the auth middleware (http.py:652-653); the 401 check (RequireAuthMiddleware) sits on the route (:614), so a guard rejects before any auth answer. fastmcp's own HostOriginGuardMiddleware (http.py:225, 421/403) is off by default (settings.py:323) and absent from the SSE app. Observed in-process and under real uvicorn with a pure-ASGI guard: evil Origin 403 (good or bad token), bad Host 421, bad/no token 401, good token initialize 200, Content-Length 9 MiB 413 with receive() called 0 times, tools/list streamed 200 text/event-stream chunked (6 chunks, 243 tools) through the guard. Endpoint path /mcp (settings.py:264). StaticTokenVerifier compares with self.tokens.get(token) (auth/providers/jwt.py:653), not constant-time.
spikes.evidence: scratchpad/spikes/s3/probe_guard.py; key lines: "middleware order: ['RequestContextMiddleware', 'AuthenticationMiddleware', 'AuthContextMiddleware', 'Guard']", 'A evil Origin + good token -> 403', 'C bad Host -> 421', 'D bad token -> 401', 'F good token + allowed Origin initialize -> 200', 'I Content-Length 9 MiB -> 413 receive() calls: 0', 'R3 uvicorn tools/list stream -> 200 text/event-stream transfer-encoding: chunked chunks: 6 tools: 243', 'R4 uvicorn 9 MiB body -> 413'.
spikes.decision: For 1.8-17(3): wrap mcp.http_app on the instance next to the existing run_async wrap (server.py:13392) so every builder (main(), mcp.run, fastmcp run, http_app()) gets Middleware(HttpGuard) prepended; the guard is pure ASGI (not BaseHTTPMiddleware), rejects on Content-Length and also counts received bytes for chunked bodies; replace StaticTokenVerifier with a small TokenVerifier subclass using hmac.compare_digest, the read-only token being the same verifier issuing an mcp:read-only scope; do not rely on fastmcp's built-in Origin/Host guard (off by default, missing from SSE). Limitation: user middleware runs after AuthenticationMiddleware, so a 403/421/413 does not reveal token validity (harmless). The instance wrap itself was not executed in the spike - same mechanism as the run_async wrap; 1.8-17's test covers it.
